description: A Bot's tasks, a page of the right-hand side panel: scripts the Bot's host keeps and runs (Python, shell, or a prompt the Bot is given as a turn), by hand or as a trigger fires (a schedule, a git push to a branch of a repo on the host), each run given its inputs filled by hand or by the trigger's event, the Bot asked mid-run when the script can't decide and handed a failed run. A task's script is the Bot's to write (its set_task tool); no app shows or edits it, and a person changes it by asking the Bot. The page goes from the list of tasks to a task's page to a run's log, each with a back button. Only exists while the open chat is a Bot; otherwise the tab is hidden, and if it was shown the panel falls back to Meta. docs/tasks-design.md has the model and the wire.
opens: the 'Tasks' tab (alarm-clock icon) in the side panel's switcher, visible only while the open chat is a Bot

parts.name: tab
parts.shows: Switcher tab with an alarm-clock icon and the label 'Tasks'; present only for a Bot chat.

parts.name: list
parts.shows: The first view: a boxed list of the Bot's tasks in the order its host keeps them, scrolling, no selection. Empty: the centred dim text 'No tasks yet'. No app makes a task here: the Bot makes its tasks (set_task), as a person asks it to. Read when the chat is opened, when a turn of the Bot ends, every 30 seconds while the page is shown (5 while a run is going), and after each change here.

parts.name: task row
parts.shows: Before the title, its last run's state icon (a tick done, a stop sign failed, a spinner running or asking, a square stopped, an arrow skipped; nothing if it has never run; its state's word as the tooltip). Title: the task's name. At the end: a switch (on = its triggers fire; tooltip 'Turn off to pause') and a Run button (play icon). No subtitle. Row text is escaped, never markup.

actions.does: pauses or resumes its triggers on the host at once (a schedule resumed is worked out afresh from now)
runs it now; a task with inputs opens the run form first

parts.name: task page
parts.shows: A header row: a back button (tooltip 'Tasks'), the task's name in bold (ellipsized), then flat buttons Run (play), Change (pencil) and Delete (trash). Below it, scrolling, a boxed list of one switch row, 'Hand failures to the Bot', then three groups each with its heading: 'Triggers', 'Inputs', 'Runs'. Each group's rows are a dense list's, as tall as a navigation list's rows: Baude's at least 36 px (1 px above and below, their buttons 24 px), as the Fixes page's; the phone's at least 38 dp, as its Fixes list's. No script and no runtime: the run page's version, and a failed run's log, are all of the script a person sees. Read when opened, every 5 seconds while a run is going, and after each change here.

actions.does: asks 'Delete <task>?' (Cancel, Delete in red, Cancel the default); Delete deletes the task on the host, with its runs and the scripts only it ran, and goes back to the list

parts.name: hand failures
parts.shows: Above the groups, its own small boxed list of one switch row titled 'Hand failures to the Bot' (no subtitle, title not markup), on while a failed run is handed to the Bot.

actions.does: saves the task at once on the host with its fallback as set, its script, runtime, inputs and triggers as they are; no dialog, no Save

decisions.said: Hand failures to the bot toggle should be on the main task page not in some pen field.
decisions.rule: Every app puts the 'Hand failures to the Bot' switch on the task's page, saved the moment it is flipped, and not in the Change Task dialog

parts.name: triggers
parts.shows: Heading 'Triggers' with a flat + at its right (tooltip 'Add trigger'). One compact row per trigger: an icon (alarm clock for a schedule, branch for a git push), the title saying what fires it ('weekdays at 09:00', 'every 2 hours', 'push to main in ~/site'), a warning icon with the trigger's last error as its tooltip if it has one, and a remove button (minus; tooltip 'Remove trigger'). No triggers: the dim line 'By hand' (every task can be run by hand).

actions.does: removes the trigger on the host at once

parts.name: inputs
parts.shows: Heading 'Inputs' with a flat pencil at its right (tooltip 'Change'). One compact row per input: title its label (or name), at the end its type in dim text (Text, Number, Yes or no, Choice). No inputs: the dim line 'No inputs'.

parts.name: runs
parts.shows: Heading 'Runs'. Its latest runs, newest first, a compact row each: the state icon, the title '<when>' on one line (HH:MM if today, else '03 Nov 14:00', on the host's clock as it was when the run started; how long it took is on the run page), and at the end an icon for what started it (alarm clock schedule, branch git push; none for a run by hand, whose run page says 'By hand') and the version, monospace, dim. No row has a play or re-run button. None: the dim line 'No runs yet'.

parts.name: run page
parts.shows: A header row: a back button (tooltip the task's name), the title '<task> · <when>' in bold, and a Wrap toggle (text-wrap icon, tooltip 'Wrap long lines', drawn pressed while on), and a Stop button (stop icon) while it's running or asking. Then one line: its state's word (or, if it failed or was stopped, why), what started it ('By hand', 'Schedule', 'Git push'), how long it took, and its version. Then, if it started any chats (one-shot agents: baude-oneshot, the mesh tools or the script library's agent, run inside it), a group headed 'Started': a boxed row per chat, its title, its state as the sessions list draws it (working grey and pulsing, waiting yellow, else done blue: they go on after the run's over, and the run's state doesn't wait for them) and a chevron. Then its log, scrolling, in order: the script's output in code blocks and its errors in code blocks of their own in the error colour (consecutive lines of each together; their long lines wrapped at the page's width while Wrap is on, else scrolled sideways), each line it said as plain text, each ask of the Bot as a card headed 'Asked <Bot>' (or 'Handed to <Bot>' for a failure handed over) with what was asked, each answer as a card headed '<Bot> answered' with the Bot's answer, what each chat it started said as a turn ended (each stopped or failed turn, then its first that finished) as a card headed '<chat> finished' (or '<chat> stopped', '<chat> failed'), a line if its Bot can't be told yet, and anything else the host says of the run as plain text. Nothing says when it started or that it ended: the title and the line under it do. Read every second while it's going, the lines since added to what's drawn.

actions.does: stops the run on the host
wraps the output and error blocks' long lines at the page's width, or scrolls them sideways again; remembered across sessions (setting task_log_wrap, on until turned off)

decisions.said: A task run's terminal-style logs need a word-wrap mode (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's run page has a Wrap toggle for its output and error blocks, as the Kubernetes logs have one: on, long lines wrap at the page's width; off, they scroll sideways. It's on until turned off, and remembered (task_log_wrap)

parts.name: message line
parts.shows: A dim wrapping line at the bottom of the page (10 px margins), hidden unless something failed: "Couldn't load the tasks.", "Couldn't run the task.", "Couldn't save the task.", "Couldn't delete the task.", "Couldn't stop the run."; the host's reason is in its tooltip. It goes away after the next successful answer.

parts.name: task dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Change Task', Cancel and Save (suggested). Content: a 'Name' field only. Not the script, not how it runs, not whether failures go to the Bot (a switch on the task's page): those are the Bot's to change or have a place of their own.

actions.does: saves its name on the host, its script, runtime, inputs, triggers and fallback as they are

parts.name: run form
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Run <task>', as the app's settings dialogs are (Change Task, a chat's Access): its inputs as one boxed list of setting rows, each titled with its label (its name if none), wrapped, with no subtitle, filled with its default: a yes/no input a switch row, a text or number input an entry row (a number's in the error colour, and Run off, while it isn't one), a choice a drop-down row of its choices. Then the buttons Cancel and Run (suggested). The phone draws the same: its boxed list, switch, entry and choice rows, Cancel and Run at the end.

actions.does: runs it with its inputs as filled

decisions.said: The run form looked ugly and unlike any of the app's other settings (paraphrased: the form shown when running a task with inputs)
decisions.rule: Every app draws a task's run form as its settings: one boxed list of rows titled with each input's label (wrapped, no subtitle), a switch row for yes/no, an entry row for text and number, a drop-down row for a choice; one suggested button, Run, beside Cancel, and no other button; a number is red from the start while its text isn't a finite number (not nan, inf, 1e999 or 1_000), an empty optional number is fine and sends nothing (the host's default stands), Enter in an entry runs the form when it's fit

parts.name: trigger dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Add Trigger', Cancel and Save. A drop-down Schedule / Git push. Schedule: 'Every' or 'At a time of day'; every: a number and minutes / hours (5 to 44640 minutes, 1 to 744 hours: what the host takes); at: 'Times in <zone>' (or 'Times on the host's clock'), an HH:MM field and seven day toggles Mon to Sun. Git push: 'Repository folder' (a path on the host) and 'Branch' (main). Then, if the task has inputs, 'Fills' and one drop-down per input, '<input> from', with 'nothing' and the trigger's payload keys (schedule: time; git push: repo, branch, before, after, commit, message, author), set to the key of the input's own name if there is one.

parts.name: inputs dialog
parts.shows: An alert dialog headed 'Change Inputs', Cancel and Save. One row per input: a 'Name' field, a type drop-down (Text, Number, Yes or no, Choice), a 'Choices, comma-separated' field shown for a choice, a 'Default' field, and a remove button (tooltip 'Remove input'); under them an 'Add input' button.

states.name: running
states.shows: A spinner before the task's name and run; the run page's Stop button

states.name: asking
states.shows: As running, its state 'asking its Bot'; the run's log ends with the ask's card

states.name: failed
states.shows: Stop-sign icon; the run's log ends with the error, and a 'Handed to <Bot>' card with the Bot's answer if it was handed over

decisions.said: Routines are rewritten as Tasks: tasks are scripts, run on a schedule or by hand at any time
decisions.rule: Every app shows a Bot's tasks where its routines were, each runnable by hand, with its triggers (a schedule among them)

decisions.said: Triggers generalise schedules; a task can be started by external events, a git push first
decisions.rule: Every app lists a task's triggers (schedule, git push) and adds or removes them on the task's page

decisions.said: A task's script can call its Bot as a fallback on errors and to handle non-deterministic steps
decisions.rule: Every app shows a run's asks of its Bot and the Bot's answers in the run's log, a failure handed over marked so

decisions.said: Input forms that triggers populate, and that the Bot can fill
decisions.rule: Every app shows a task's inputs, fills them before a run by hand, and lets a trigger map its payload onto them

decisions.said: Telemetry includes when triggers happen, how long scripts take, failures and version hashes
decisions.rule: Every app lists a task's runs with when, what started it, how it ended and the version it ran, and a run's page says how long it took

decisions.said: For tasks UI, users probably don't need to see scripts at all these are probably going to blow up to pretty complex apps in the bot git repo.
decisions.rule: No app shows a task's script or lets a person edit it, nor its runtime: the Bot writes and changes scripts (set_task), and a person asks the Bot to. A task's version stays on its runs and its run page; a run's log (tracebacks too) shows as it is
Every app calls a task's fields its Inputs: the task page's group, its dialog (Change Inputs), its rows and buttons (Add input, Remove input). The wire keeps the field's name, form

decisions.said: Form row height should ne narrower as should triggrs and runs
decisions.rule: Every app draws a task's Inputs, Triggers and Runs as dense lists, but not thinner than its navigation lists' rows: Baude's 36 px (libadwaita's navigation-sidebar row, as the Fixes page and Record's notebooks have), the phone's 38 dp (as its Fixes list); not the 26 px sessions-list row, nor a full list row

decisions.said:
* We probably want some kind of environment variable given to tasks that causes baude oneshot agents spawned to nest themselves underneath the bot.
* We also probably want oneshot agents laucnhed by the task to be associated with that task, if a task triggers a oneshot agent, there's a sense in which it's still running. Not sure wht the ideal situation is here. As somtimes if you have some complex chain of tasks, yes, indeed the first phase is not running. We don't have this yet so it should be fine.
decisions.rule: A one-shot agent a task's run starts (baude-oneshot, the mesh tools, the script library's agent) nests under the run's Bot in every app's sessions list, is kept with the run (Started on its page) and links back to it (its first message's from line). A run is over when its script ends: the chats it started go on, their live states shown under Started

decisions.said: * Philosophy: I have a deployment tak that fallsback to a oneshot agent when teh deploy fails. But the oneshot agent spawned outside of the bot which is not ideal, and did not keep in touch with the bot either.
decisions.rule: As a chat a task's run started ends its first turn (or stops, or fails), its Bot is sent what it said, as a message from that chat whose from line links to it, and the run's log says it too

decisions.said: Dont really like how the oneshot messages mix. agent text and template text
decisions.rule: A chat a task's run started reports each turn that's stopped or fails, and its first that finishes, to its Bot as a message of only its own words; the run's log has the same as a card headed "<chat> finished" (or stopped, failed), and the run's page stops looking for them once each chat it started has finished a turn, or an hour after the run's over. A run opened from a from line opens its task's page under it, so Back goes to that task

decisions.said: The rows in Tasks are too thin; make them a little taller (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app draws a task's Inputs, Triggers and Runs as dense lists, but not thinner than its navigation lists' rows: Baude's 36 px (libadwaita's navigation-sidebar row, as the Fixes page and Record's notebooks have), the phone's 38 dp (as its Fixes list); not the 26 px sessions-list row, nor a full list row

removed.name: The play icon at the end of a run's row (a run started by hand)
removed.why: It looked like a button to run that run again. The owner: "I'm never going to re-run older runs. Drop the play button from the rows." A run's row has no play or re-run control; the task's own Run (its list row and its page) starts a new run. The host keeps run_task, which that Run uses

removed.name: Script group on a task's page, and the script and runtime in the task dialog
removed.why: The owner: "users probably don't need to see scripts at all these are probably going to blow up to pretty complex apps in the bot git repo." Scripts are the Bot's to write (set_task)

removed.name: New task button (+) on the tasks list, and the New Task dialog
removed.why: A consequence of no scripts in the UI: the host takes no task without a script; scripts are the Bot's to write. A person asks the Bot for a new task

removed.name: Run with dummy answers (the run form's button, a run's ' · dry' tag and 'dummy answers' fact, run_task's dry)
removed.why: The owner called Run with dummy answers a terrible feature and asked for it to go (paraphrased). Every app runs a task only for real: no button, tag or wire flag for a run whose asks a dummy agent answers
